title: Baking soda on its own for baking powder

evidence.basis: B1. OD-7 (owner commission 2026-10-08, ENGINEERING only; not culinary validation, not released guidance). Evidence: private/research/substitution-knowledge (2026-10-07). Bob's Red Mill SRC-LV-10#f (soda lacks the acid to make it rise); Arm & Hammer SRC-LV-09#e (about 3-4 times as strong; bitter or soapy). Scope: no acid in the recipe (applicability; an unconfirmed ingredient leaves it unknown). A recipe reformulated around soda and an acid is outside it.

text: Baking soda on its own can't stand in for the baking powder in this recipe: soda needs an acid to make the dough rise, nothing here supplies one, and it's about 3 to 4 times as strong, so a like-for-like swap tastes soapy.
scopeNote: This is about baking soda alone in this recipe as written. A recipe developed around soda and an acid is different, and so is soda with cream of tartar.
answer: on its own can't make this dough rise
